maya (PM): quick pre-handoff gap-scan — we need a concise check on SLA coverage, monitoring, support burn-in, and pricing backstops before we go prod.
devin (SRE): on it. what's the canonical SLA target we're committing to? p95/p99/availability?
maya (PM): aiming for p95 <= 150ms for inference, p99 <= 400ms for non-burst, availability 99.95%. also define error budget runout policy.
lucas (ProdOps): noted. need to confirm autoscale burst lanes and reserved capacity failover. if traffic spikes x3, fallback model path must be tested.
rahul (FinOps): pricing question: do we expose burst surcharge or throttle? need a fallback pricing blob for pilot customers.
emily (Support): we need runbooks for: 1) model degradation (quality regression), 2) latency spikes, 3) billing disputes. who owns each?
anna (Docs): i'll draft quickstart and runbook stubs. can we get a prioritized checklist of the user journeys we must document?
maya (PM): priority: self-serve dev onboarding, enterprise SLA signup flow, and incident RCA template. also add examples for dedicated/private config.
devin (SRE): infra checks: alerting thresholds, dashboards, and P95 SLO Burn Rate alert. propose alerts: `burn_rate > 2 for 1h` and `p95 > 150ms for 5m`.
oncall-bot: Deploy notice: prod-serving/v1.9 deployed to us-west-2 at 2024-07-10T14:01Z.
lucas (ProdOps): Devin, can you add a synthetic traffic job for mix of short/long seqs to validate p99 tails under burst? schedule nightly for 72h.
devin (SRE): yes, I'll add a k8s CronJob + integration with perf-dashboard. will post log links.
rahul (FinOps): for pricing: suggest two options for pilot customers: 1) burst credit with surcharge, 2) throttled tier with lower base price. want numbers by EOD.
emily (Support): assigning owners: model quality -> research oncall, latency incidents -> infra oncall, billing disputes -> billing ops (rahul).
anna (Docs): I'll create PRs: /docs/quickstart, /docs/sla, /docs/troubleshooting. need sample payloads and expected token counts for cost calc.
maya (PM): action list: 1) SRE: alert + synthetic (devin). 2) ProdOps: failover tests + capacity plan (lucas). 3) Docs: runbook/quickstart (anna). 4) FinOps: pricing options (rahul). 5) Support: runbook owners + escalation (emily). due: EOD tomorrow.
devin (SRE): will add alert rules and send a draft dashboard link before EOD.
lucas (ProdOps): I'll schedule failover tests for tomorrow morning and add results to the runbook.
rahul (FinOps): drafting pricing options now; will attach simple spreadsheet with sensitivity cases.
emily (Support): I'll draft runbook flows and escalation matrices; want a dry-run with oncall next week.
maya (PM): perfect. last ask: include explicit SLA exception process and commercial escalation path in the docset.
anna (Docs): will include template emails and contract language snippet for exceptions.
oncall-bot: Reminder: PagerDuty maintenance window 2024-07-11 02:00-03:00 UTC.
maya (PM): thanks team — we'll reconvene tomorrow 09:30 PT for a final go/no-go readout. :thumbsup:
